title: Harry Tarzan's band and early Roadhouse-era players
summary: What Harold remembers of Harry Tarzan, clarinet, and the musicians around him before the roadhouse job.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Oh yes, oh, well played a little bit. I know almost nothing about him. Well, Harry Tarzan played, before I went out to the, uh, uh, the, uh, the, uh, the, uh, before I played before I had a band out at the, uh, Roadhouse out there, I heard him playing with a band and I think he was playing with- Jules Cherzaud was playing piano. I think Mary Brunesse was playing cornet in them days, Harry Tarzan clarinet. And I think it was George Treey on drums, played fine drums. one of my dad's students who played fine. He played in the theaters too, he played in the theater. But I remember they played out there sometime there and Harry taught them play. Yeah, Harry played good clarinet and he had a band over in Block City, I don't remember. A fellow by the name of Dick Pitcher used to play cornet with him. I don't know him. Oh, none of the guys know him pretty well, but he played some new arms here. And Jeff Reddick's brother played piano with him, Johnny Reddick, Harry, Luke Dubas, I believe his folks was in the oyster business over there, you know. Yeah, I think he played drums.
